title: Selection, Phenotyping, Progeny Testing and Trait Stability

content.overview: Selection changes a breeding population only when chosen individuals contribute to later generations. Strong selection requires defined traits, repeatable phenotyping, environmental records, adequate population size, and progeny evidence to distinguish attractive one-time expression from stable inheritance.

vocabulary.definition: Systematic measurement or description of observable traits.
The degree to which certain individuals are favored over others for reproduction.
Evaluation of offspring to learn how reliably a parent's traits are transmitted.
Consistency of trait inheritance or expression across relevant generations and environments.

sections.title: Selection begins with a defined target
sections.body: Traits should be specified before choosing parents so the breeder is not simply selecting whichever individual looks most impressive at the end.

sections.title: Phenotype includes environment
sections.body: Observed traits reflect genotype, development, and environment. Replication or repeated evaluation helps prevent environmental advantage from being mistaken for superior inheritance.

sections.title: Progeny reveal inheritance
sections.body: A selected parent is valuable only if desirable traits are transmitted in useful combinations. Progeny testing provides stronger evidence than the parent's phenotype alone.

sections.title: Stability takes generations
sections.body: Uniform or repeated expression usually requires continued selection and evaluation. A trait observed once should not be called fixed without evidence from later generations.

workedExamples: If a plant has exceptional aroma but its offspring rarely express similar chemistry, the parent phenotype alone did not predict stable transmission.
If one candidate was grown in a brighter corner, compare environmental records before ranking it above genetically related plants.
commonMistakes: Changing selection criteria after seeing the population.
Selecting from phenotype without environmental notes.
Calling a line stable after one generation.
Failing to keep rejected as well as selected records.
content.practicalApplication: Create a selection sheet with trait definitions, measurement method, parentage, generation, environment, scores, selection decision, and later progeny results. Use the same definitions across generations.
content.summary: Breeding selection is a recorded experiment. Defined traits, environmental context, progeny testing, and repeated generations are what turn attractive individuals into evidence of heritable progress.
